# AI use statement {.unnumbered}

We used AI coding agents and assistants (Claude, Codex and Cursor) extensively in
this work. They wrote and ran experiment code, managed jobs on a remote workstation,
aggregated results, generated the figures from the committed result files, and drafted
and edited manuscript text. Research questions, experimental designs and decision rules
were discussed with the agents. After the initial couplet split, every design and decision rule was committed
to version control before the corresponding result was computed. The authors reviewed the code, the committed
results and every claim in the manuscript. Numbers in the text were checked against
the machine-readable result files, and citations were checked against their sources. We take responsibility for the final content of this work, including
text, claims and artifacts produced with the aid of generative AI.

# Ethics statement {.unnumbered}

This work studies how openly released language models use information they have
not written. Its aim is to support the monitoring of such models. It involves no
human subjects, personal data or harmful content. The hidden-choice task elicits
harmless secret choices (fruits, animals). The results locate where content that the
text does not reveal is stored, which is information useful to monitors. We do not
see a plausible route by which it helps a model conceal content. The limitations
section states where the findings may not transfer, notably to long reasoning with
thinking enabled. The discussion notes that training which rewards concealment is
untested.

# Reproducibility statement {.unnumbered}

All experiments use publicly released checkpoints (Appendix @sec-app-materials) and
public prompts released by @hanna2026latent [@hanna2026planningdata] (used in their chat format and in the plain template of @ma2026plan) or generated with fixed seeds. Upon acceptance we will release the code and result files on
GitHub. That release will contain, for every experiment, the code, the per-item
result rows and summaries with bootstrap intervals, and the scripts that generate
every figure and table from those files. After the initial couplet split, it will
also contain each design and decision rule as committed before the corresponding
result. The log of committed decision rules (Appendix @sec-app-prereg) lists each
frozen design, its decision rule and the outcome. Dated deviations are recorded
with each experiment, and the main ones are listed there. Batched edits and
generation were checked against unbatched reference implementations (Appendix
@sec-app-materials). Compute is described in Appendix @sec-app-compute.
